definition: A machine that carries people up and down between the floors of a building.
example: We took the lift to the fifth floor.
note: Was defined as 'to raise something', which made it an exact copy of the entry for 'raise'. In British English the first meaning of 'lift' is the machine you ride between floors, so the entry now teaches that and the duplication disappears.

definition: To send a letter or parcel by post.
example: I will mail the letter tomorrow afternoon.
note: Italian was a whole phrase ('spedire posta o email') instead of a single word. Shortened to 'spedire'.

definition: Very large or very important.
example: There is a major problem with the plan.
note: Had been turned into the American university expression 'to major in a subject'. All three original translations were the describing word meaning 'important', which is the first meaning of 'major'. Restored.

definition: To be important.
example: It does not matter if you are a little late.
note: The entry taught 'matter' as the physical substance of the universe, with the strange example 'The book is made of matter'. In everyday English 'matter' means 'to be important', as in 'it doesn't matter'. Completely rebuilt.

definition: Used to say that something is possible but not certain.
example: I might go to the park later if the weather is nice.
note: Spanish gave an adverb ('maybe') and Italian gave the 'I' form while the others gave the 'he/she' form. All four now match.

definition: To have to have something because it is necessary.
example: I need water to drink and stay alive.
note: The definition itself was not correct English ('to must have something'). Rewritten.

definition: Us and no one else.
example: We painted the house ourselves.
note: Italian was the women-only form ('noi stesse'); changed to the normal form. German was incomplete on its own.

definition: A style of modern popular music.
example: She listens to pop music every day.
note: Had been turned into the sound a balloon makes. Three of the four original translations were the music style, which is what everyone thinks of first. Restored.

definition: A competition to see who is the fastest.
example: He won the race and received a gold medal.
note: All three original translations were the event itself, and the model had changed them into the action of racing. The first meaning of 'race' is the event. Restored.

definition: The speed at which something happens, or how often it happens.
example: The population is growing at a fast rate.
note: Italian 'ritmo' means rhythm and did not match the other three. Changed to 'tasso'. The example used awkward English ('a high rate of speed') and has been rewritten.

definition: To move upward, especially the sun coming up in the morning.
example: The sun will rise in the east every morning.
note: All four translations are the special words used for the sun rising, but the definition just said 'to move upward', so they looked wrong. The definition now matches them.

definition: In a way that shows sadness.
example: She sadly walked away.
note: French 'malheureusement' means 'unfortunately', which is a different idea. Changed to 'tristement' to match the other three.

definition: To rescue someone or something from danger.
example: The firefighter saved the child from the burning house.
note: The entry only taught the narrow computer meaning ('save the document'). The first meaning of 'save' is to rescue, which is what the original French and Italian showed. Rebuilt around that.

definition: The number of points won in a game or test.
example: His score improved after weeks of practice.
note: Spanish 'puntaje' is mainly Latin American; 'puntuación' is understood everywhere.

definition: Used to ask about or suggest a future action.
example: Shall we begin?
note: German gave a conjugated form while the other three gave the base form. Now all four match.

definition: Only one; not more than one.
example: There was a single apple left in the bowl.
note: German 'einzel' is only half a word. Spanish 'sencillo' means 'simple'. The example was about a one-way ticket, which is a different meaning, so it has been replaced with one that shows 'only one'.

definition: How big or small something is.
example: The size is too large.
note: Italian 'taglia' only means clothing size. The general word is 'dimensione'.

definition: A device that sound comes out of.
example: The music sounded great through the new speakers.
note: Had been changed to 'a person talking to an audience'. Three of the four original translations were the audio device, which is the everyday object a learner meets first. Restored.

definition: A small piece of paper you stick on a letter to send it by post.
example: I need a stamp for the letter.
note: Spanish 'estampilla' is mainly Latin American; 'sello' is understood everywhere.

definition: A word or phrase used for one particular thing.
example: 'Photosynthesis' is a scientific term.
note: Had been changed to mean a part of the school year. The original German and French were both 'a word or expression', which is the first meaning of 'term'. All four now match.

definition: The act of using your mind to form ideas.
example: Clear thinking helps you solve difficult problems.
note: Spanish had been changed to a half-verb form while the other three stayed as the thing itself. Spanish restored, and the example now shows the thing rather than the action.
